chapters: Adam, Shes, Enosh.
Keinan, Mahalalel, Yered.
Hanoch, Mesushelach, Lemech.
Noach, Shem, Cham, and Yefes.
The sons of Yefes: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Yavan, and Tuval, and Meshech, and Tiras.
And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Diphath, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Yavan: Elishah and Tarshishah, Kittim, and Rodanim.
The sons of Cham: Kush and Mitzrayim, Put and Kena'an.
And the sons of Kush: Seba, and Havilah, and Sabta, and Raama, and Sabtecha; and the sons of Raama: Sheva and Dedan.
And Kush begot Nimrod; he began to be a mighty man on the earth.
And Mitzrayim begot Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehavim, and Naftuchim.
And Patrusim and Kasluchim, from whom the Pelishtim and the Kaftorim were descended.
And Kena'an begot Tzidon his firstborn and Heth.
And the Yevusi[s], and the Emori[s], and the Girgashi[s].
And the Chivi[s], and the Arki[s], and the Sini[s].
And the Arvadi[s], and the Tzemari[s], and the Chamasi[s].
The sons of Shem: Eilam, and Ashur, and Arpachshad, and Lud, and Aram, and Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Meshech.
And Arpachshad begot Shelach, and Shelach begot Eiver.
And to Eiver were born two sons; one was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was parted and his brother's name was Yoktan.
And Yoktan begot Almodad, and Shaleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Yorah.
And Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah.
And Ebal, and Abimael, and Sheva.
And Ofir, and Havilah, and Yobab; all these were the sons of Yoktan.
Shem, Arpachshad, Shelach.
Eiver, Peleg, Re'u.
Serug, Nachor, Terach.
Avram, he is Avraham.
The sons of Avraham: Yitzchak and Yishmael.
These are their generations: the firstborn of Yishmael was Nebaioth, and Kedar, and Adbeal, and Mibsam.
Mishma, and Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema.
Yetur, Naphish, and Kedmah; all these were the sons of Yishmael.
And the sons of Keturah, Avraham's concubine; she bore Zimran, and Yokshan, and Medan, and Midyan, and Yishbak, and Shuah; and the sons of Yokshan: Sheva and Dedan.
And the sons of Midyan: Eifah, and Efer, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah; all these were the sons of Keturah.
And Avraham begot Yitzchak; the sons of Yitzchak: Eisav and Yisroel.
The sons of Eisav: Elifaz, Reuel, and Jeush, and Yaalam, and Korach.
The sons of Elifaz: Teman, and Omar, Zephi, and Gaatam, Kenaz, and Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shamah, and Mizzah.
And the sons of Seir: Lotan, and Shoval, and Zibeon, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan.
And the sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam, and Lotan's sister was Timna.
The sons of Shoval: Alian, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shephi, and Onam, and the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
The sons of Anah: Dishon, and the sons of Dishon: Hamran, and Eshban, and Yisran, and Cheran.
The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, and Zaavan, Yaakan; the sons of Dishon: Uz and Aran.
Now these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Children of Yisroel: Bela the son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
And Bela died, and Yobab the son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his stead.
And Yobab died, and Chusham from the land of the Teimani[s] reigned in his stead.
And Chusham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote Midyan in the field of Moav, reigned in his stead, and the name of his city was Avith.
And Hadad died and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.
And Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.
And Shaul died, and Baal Chanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.
And Baal Chanan died, and Hadad reigned in his stead. Now the name of his city was Pai, and his wife's name was Mehetabel the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
And Hadad died, and the chiefs of Edom were: Chief Timna, Chief Alvah, Chief Yeses.
Chief Oholibamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinnon.
Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mibzar.
Chief Magdiel, Chief Iram; these were the chiefs of Edom.
These are the sons of Yisroel: Reuven, Shimon, Levi, and Yehudah, Yissachar, and Zevulun.
Dan, Yosef, and Binyamin, Naftali, Gad, and Asher.

The sons of Yehudah: Er, and Onan, and Shelach. Three were born to him from the daughter of Shua, the Kena'ani, and Er, the firstborn of Yehudah, was evil in the eyes of Havayah, and He put him to death.
And Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bore him Peretz and Zerah; all the sons of Yehudah were five.
The sons of Peretz: Hezron and Hamul.
And the sons of Zerah: Zimri, and Eitan, and Heiman, and Calcol, and Dara; all of them five.
And the sons of Karmi: Achar, the troubler of Yisroel, who committed a trespass in the consecrated property.
And the sons of Eitan: Azaryah.
And the sons of Hezron, who were born to him: Yerahmeel, and Ram, and Kelubai.
And Ram begot Amminadab, and Amminadab begot Nahshon, the prince of the children of Yehudah.
And Nahshon begot Salma, and Salma begot Boaz.
And Boaz begot Obed, and Obed begot Yishai.
And Ishai begot his firstborn, Eliab, and Abinadab, the second one, and Shimea, the third one.
Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth.
Ozem the sixth, Dovid the seventh.
And their sisters: Zeruyah and Avigayil, and the sons of Zeruyah: Abshai, and Yoav, and Asael; three.
And Avigayil bore Amasa, and the father of Amasa was Yeser the Ishmaeli.
And Kalev the son of Hezron begot Azubah-Ishah and Yerios, and these were her sons: Yesher, and Shovav, and Ardon.
And Azubah died, and Kalev took to himself Efras, and she bore him Hur.
And Hur begot Uri, and Uri begot Bezalel.
And afterwards, Hezron came to the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilad, and he took her, and he was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub.
And Segub begot Yair, and he had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilad.
And Geshur and Aram took the villages of Yair from them; with Kenath and its villages, sixty cities; all these [belonged to] the sons of Machir, the father of Gilad.
And after the death of Hezron in Kalev Efrasah, and the wife of Hezron was Aviyah, and she bore him Ashhur, the father of Tekoa.
And the sons of Yerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron were: the firstborn was Ram, and Bunah, and Oren, and Ozem, [and] Achiyah.
Now Yerahmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Onam.
And the sons of Ram, the firstborn of Yerahmeel: Maaz, and Yamin, and Eker.
And the sons of Onam were: Shamai and Yada, and the sons of Shamai: Nadab and Abishur.
Now the name of the wife of Abishur was Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
And the sons of Nadab were Seled and Appaim, and Seled died without children.
And the sons of Appaim: Ishi, and the sons of Ishi: Sheshan, and the sons of Sheshan: Ahlai.
And the sons of Yada the brother of Shamai: Yeser and Yonasan, and Yeser died without children.
And the sons of Yonasan: Peleth and Zaza; these were the sons of Yerahmeel.
And Sheshan had no sons but daughters, and Sheshan had a Mitzri slave named Yarcha.
And Sheshan gave his daughter to Yarcha his slave for a wife, and she bore him Attai.
And Attai begot Nasan, and Nasan begot Zabad.
And Zabad begot Eflal, and Eflal begot Obed.
And Obed begot Yehu, and Yehu begot Azaryah.
And Azaryah begot Helez, and Helez begot Elasah.
And Elasah begot Sismai, and Sismai begot Shalum.
And Shalum begot Yekamyah, and Yekamyah begot Elishama.
And the sons of Kalev, the brother of Yerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn; he was the father of Zif and the inhabitants of Mareshah, the father of Chevron.
And the sons of Chevron: Korach, and Tappuah, and Rekem, and Shama.
And Shema begot Raham, the father of Yorkeam, and Rekem begot Shamai.
And Shamai's son was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beis-Zur.
And Eifah, the concubine of Kalev, bore Charan, and Moza, and Gazez and Charan begot Gazez.
And the sons of Yechdai: Regem, and Yosam, and Geshan, and Pelet, and Eifah, and Shaaph.
[From] Kalev's concubine, Maacah, he begot Sheber and Tirhanah.
And she bore Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbenah and the father of Givah; and Kalev's daughter was Achsah.
These were the sons of Kalev the son of Hur, the firstborn of Efrasah: Shoval the father of Kiryas-Yearim.
Salma the father of Beis Lechem, Hareph the father of Beis-Gader.
And Shoval the father of Kiryas-Yearim, who ruled over half the Menuhoth, had sons.
And the families of Kiryas-Yearim: the Yisrim, and the Pusim, and the Shumathim, and the Mishrathim; from these came the Tzorasim and the Eshtaolim.
The sons of Salma: Beis Lechem, and the Netofasim, Atroth Beis-Yoav, and half the Manahtim, [and] the Tzorasim.
And the families of scholars, those who dwelt with Yabetz: Tirathim, Shimathim, Suchathim; they are the Keinim, who were descended from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
And these were the sons of Dovid who were born to him in Chevron: the firstborn, Amnon, to Ahinoam the Yizreelis; the second, Daniel, to Avigayil the Carmelis.
The third, Avshalom, the son of Maacah, the daughter of Talmai the king of Geshur: the fourth, Adoniyah, the son of Haggith.
The fifth, Shefatyah, to Abital; the sixth, Ithream, to Eglah his wife.
Six were born to him in Chevron, and he reigned there seven years and six months, and thirty-three years he reigned in Yerushalayim.
And these were born to him in Yerushalayim: Shimea, and Shovav, and Nasan, and Shlomo-four, to Bath Shua the daughter of Ammiel.
And Ibhar, and Elishama, and Eliphelet.
And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Yafia.
And Elishama, and Elijada and Eliphelet-nine.
All the sons of Dovid, besides the sons of the concubines and Tamar their sister.
And the son of Shlomo was Rechavam, Aviyah his son, Asa his son, Yehoshafat his son.
Yoram his son, Achazyah his son, Yoash his son.
Amatzyah his son, Azaryah his son, Yosam his son.
Achaz his son, Chizkiyah his son, Menasheh his son.
Amon his son, Yoshiyah his son.
And the sons of Yoshiyah: the firstborn Yochanan, the second Yehoyakim, the third Tzidkiyah, the fourth Shalum.
And the sons of Yehoyakim: Yechonyah his son, Tzidkiyah his son.
And the sons of Yechonyah: Assir, Shealtiel his son.
And Malciram, and Pedayah, and Shenatzar, Yekamyah, Hoshama and Nedavyah.
And the sons of Pedayah: Zerubavel and Shimi, and the son[s] of Zerubavel: Meshullam, and Chananyah, and Shelomis their sister.
And Hashubah, and Ohel, and Berechyah, and Chasadyah, Yushav-Hesed-five.
And the son[s] of Chananyah: Pelatyah and Yeshayah; his son was Refayah; his son was Arnan; his son was Ovadyah; his son was Shechanyah.
And the sons of Shechanyah: Shemayah, and the sons of Shemayah: Hattush, and Yigal, and Beriah, and Nearyah, and Shafat-six.
And the son[s] of Nearyah; Eljoenai, and Chizkiyah, and Azrikam-three.
And the sons of Eljoenai; Hodavyah, and Eliashib, and Pelayah, and Akkub, and Yochanan, and Delayah, and Anani-seven.
The sons of Yehudah; Peretz, Hezron, and Karmi, and Hur, and Shoval.
And Reayah the son of Shoval begot Yahath, and Yahath begot Ahumai and Lahad; these are the families of the Tzorasim.
And these are [the sons of Hur]; Abi-Etam, Yizreel, and Ishma, and Idbash, and the name of their sister was Hazzelelponi.
And Penuel, the father of Gedor, and Ezer, the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Efrasah, the father of Beis Lechem.
And Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah.
And Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, and Hepher, and Temeni, and Haahashtari. These are the sons of Naarah.
And the sons of Helah: Zereth, and Zohar, and Ethnan.
And Koz begot Anub and Hazzobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.
Now Yabetz was more esteemed than his brothers, and his mother named him Yabetz, saying, "For I bore him in sadness."

And Yabetz called out to the Elokim of Yisroel, saying, "If You bless me and increase my border, and Your hand is with me that You save me from harm, so as not to grieve me," and Elokim fulfilled that which he had requested.
And Celub, the brother of Shuhah, begot Mehir; he is the father of Eshton.
And Eshton begot Beis-rapha, and Paseah, and Tehinnah, the leader of Ir-Nahash; these are the people of Rechah.
And the sons of Kenaz: Osniel and Serayah, and the sons of Osniel: Hathath.
And Meonothai begot Ophrah, and Serayah begot Yoav, the leader of Gei Harashim (the valley of craftsmen), for they were craftsmen.
And the sons of Kalev the son of Yefuneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam, and the sons of Elah: Uknaz.
And the sons of Yehallel: Zif, and Ziphah, Tiryah, and Asarel.
And the son[s] of Ezrah: Yeser, and Mered, and Efer, and Yalon, and she conceived Miriam, and Shamai, and Ishbah, the father of Eshtemoa.
And his wife the Yehudis bore Yered, the father of Gedor, and Heber the father of Soco, and Yekusiel, the father of Zanoah. And these are the sons of Bisyah the daughter of Paroh, whom Mered married.
And the sons of the wife of Hodiyah, the sister of Naham: the father of Keilah the Garmi and Eshtemoa the Maachasi.
And the sons of Shimon: Amnon, and Rinnah, Ben-Chanan, and Tilon, and the sons of Ishi: Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.
The sons of Shelach the son of Yehudah: Er, the father of Lechah, and Ladah, the father of Mareshah, and the families of Beis-Abodath Habbuz of the house of Ashbea.
And Yokim and the people of Kozeba, and Yoash, and Saraph, who married in Moav, and Yashuvi-Lehem, and the matters are ancient.
They, the potters and the dwellers in plantations and hedges with the king in his work, dwelt there.
The sons of Shimon: Nemuel, and Yamin, Yariv, Zerah, Shaul.
Shalum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son.
And the sons of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimi his son.
And Shimi had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many sons, and all their family did not multiply as much as the children of Yehudah.
They dwelt in Be'er Sheva, and Moladah, and Hazar Shual.
And in Bilhah, and in Ezem, and in Tolad.
And in Betuel, and in Hormah, and in Tziklag.
And in Beis Marcaboth, and in Hazar-Susim, and in Beis-Biri, and in Shaaraim; these were their cities until Dovid reigned.
And their villages: Etam and Ain, Rimmon, and Tochen, and Ashan-five cities.
And all their villages that were around these cities up to Baal; this was [the account] of their settlements, and they had their genealogical records.
And Meshobab, and Yamlech, and Joshah the son of Amatzyah.
And Yoel, and Yehu the son of Yoshivyah, the son of Serayah, the son of Asiel.
And Eljoenai, and Yaakovah, and Yeshochayah, and Asayah, and Adiel, and Yesimiel, and Benayahu.
And Ziza the son of Shiphi, and Allon the son of Yedayah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemayah.
These mentioned by name were princes in their families, and their fathers' house spread exceedingly.
And they went to the entrance of Gedor until the east of the valley to seek pasture for their sheep.
And they found fat and good pasture, and the land was spacious, and quiet, and tranquil, for the dwellers of yore were from Cham.

And these recorded by names in the days of King Yechezkyah of Yehudah came, and they smote their tents and the dwellings that were found there, and they destroyed them to this very day and dwelt instead of them, because there was pasture for their sheep there.
And of them, five hundred men of the children of Shimon went to Mount Seir, and Pelatyah and Nearyah, and Refayah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi at their head.
And they smote the remnant of the Amalekim that had escaped, and they dwelt there to this day.

And the sons of Reuven, the firstborn of Yisroel, for he was the firstborn, but when he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Yosef the son of Yisroel, but not to be reckoned in the genealogy as firstborn.
Because Yehudah prevailed over his brothers, and the one appointed as prince was to be from him, but the birthright belonged to Yosef.
The sons of Reuven, the firstborn of Yisroel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Karmi.
The sons of Yoel: Shemayah his son, Gog his son, Shimi his son.
Michah his son, Reayah his son, Baal his son.
Beerah his son, whom Tillegath-Pilneser, the king of Ashur, exiled — he was the prince of the Reuvenim.
And his companions, [each one] to his families, tracing their genealogy to their generations; the heads were Yeiel, and Zecharyah.
And Bela the son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Yoel; he dwelled in Aroer and until Nebo and Baal-Meon.
And eastward, he dwelled until the approach to the desert from the Peras River, for their cattle multiplied in the land of Gilad.
And in the days of Shaul, they made war with the Hagarim, and they fell into their hands, and they dwelt in their tents over the entire face of the east of Gilad.
And the sons of Gad dwelt opposite them in the land of Bashan until Salcah.
Yoel was the head, and Shapham was the second in command, and Yanai, and Shaphat in Bashan.
And their brothers to the house of their fathers: Michoel, and Meshullam, and Sheva, and Yorai, and Yakan, and Zia, and Eiver-seven.
These are the sons of Abihail, the son of Huri, the son of Yaroach, the son of Gilad, the son of Michoel, the son of Yeshishai, the son of Yachdo, the son of Buz.
Ahi the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni was the head of the house of their fathers.
And they dwelt in Gilad, in Bashan, and in its villages, and in all the suburbs of Sharon until their limits.
They all traced their genealogy in the days of Yosam, king of Yehudah and in the days of Yeravam, king of Yisroel.

The sons of Reuven, and the Gadim, and half the tribe of Menasheh-of men of valor, men who bear shields and swords and draw the bow, and who are trained for war, forty-four thousand, seven hundred and sixty, going out to war.
And they made war with the Hagarim, and Yetur, and Naphish, and Nodab.

And they were assisted against them, and the Hagarim and all who were with them were delivered into their hands, for they cried out to Elokim in the battle, and He accepted their prayers because they trusted in Him.
And they captured their cattle, their camels fifty thousand, and flocks two hundred and fifty thousand, and donkeys two thousand, and human beings one hundred thousand.
For many fell slain, for the battle was from Elokim, and they dwelt in their place until the exile.
And the sons of half the tribe of Menasheh dwelt in the land; from Bashan until Baal-Hermon and Senir and Mount Hermon they multiplied.
And these are the heads of their fathers' house: Efer, and Ishei, and Eliel, and Azriel, and Yirmeyah, and Hodavyah, and Yachdiel, mighty men of valor, famous men, heads of their fathers' house.
And they betrayed the Elokim of their fathers, and they strayed after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom Elokim had destroyed before them.

And Elokim inspired Pul the king of Ashur and Tillegath-Pilneser the king of Ashur, and they exiled the Reuvenim, the Gadim, and half the tribe of Menasheh, and brought them to Halah, and Habor, and Hara, and the Gozan River until this day.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kehath, and Merari.
And the sons of Kehath: Amram, Izhar, and Chevron, and Uzziel.
And the children of Amram: Aharon, and Moshe, and Miriam, and the sons of Aharon: Nadab, and Abihu, Elazar, and Ithamar.
Elazar begot Pinchas: Pinchas begot Abishua.
And Abishua begot Bukki, and Bukki begot Uzzi.
And Uzzi begot Zerachyah, and Zerachyah begot Meraioth.
Meraioth begot Amaryah, and Amaryah begot Ahitub.
And Ahitub begot Tzadok, and Tzadok begot Achimaatz.
And Achimaatz begot Azaryah, and Azaryah begot Yochanan.
And Yochanan begot Azaryah; he is the one who served in the Temple that Shlomo built in Yerushalayim.
And Azaryah begot Amaryah, and Amaryah begot Ahitub.
And Ahitub begot Tzadok, and Tzadok begot Shalum.
And Shalum begot Chilkiyah, and Chilkiyah begot Azaryah.
And Azaryah begot Seryah, and Seryah begot Yehozadak.
And Yehozadak went when Havayah exiled Yehudah and Yerushalayim by the hand of Nevuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kehath, and Merari.
And these are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimi.
And the sons of Kehath: Amram, and Izhar, and Chevron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi, and these are the families of the Leviim to their fathers.
To Gershom; Libni his son, Yahath his son, Zimmah his son.
Yoah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, Yeasrai his son.
The sons of Kehath: Amminadab his son, Korach his son, Assir his son.
Elkanah his son, and Ebiasaph his son, and Assir his son.
Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uziyah his son, and Shaul his son.
And the sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth.
Elkanah — the sons of Elkanah; Zophai his son and Nahath his son.
Eliab his son, Yerocham his son, Elkanah his son.
And the sons of Shmuel: the firstborn was Vashni and Aviyah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimi his son, Uzzah his son.
Shimea his son, Chagiyah his son, Asayah his son.
And these are the ones that Dovid stationed to sing in the House of Havayah since the Ark was deposited.
And they were ministering before the Tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting with song until Shlomo built the House of Havayah in Yerushalayim, and they stood according to their custom at their service.
And these are those who stood [at their stations] and their sons; of the sons of the Kehasim, Heiman the singer, the son of Yoel, the son of Shmuel.
The son of Elkanah, the son of Yerocham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah.
The son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai.
The son of Elkanah, the son of Yoel, the son of Azaryah, the son of Tzefanyah.
The son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korach.
The son of Izhar, the son of Kehath, the son of Levi, the son of Yisroel.
And his brother Asaf, who stood at his right, Asaf the son of Berechyah, the son of Shimea.
The son of Michoel, the son of Baasyah, the son of Malkiyah.
The son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adayah.
The son of Eitan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimi.
The son of Yahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.
And the sons of Merari their brethren were on the left; Eitan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch.
The son of Chashavyah, the son of Amatzyah, the son of Chilkiyah.
The son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer.
The son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.
And their brethren the Leviim were appointed for the entire service of the Tabernacle of the House of Elokim.

And Aharon and his sons were offering on the altar of the burnt offerings and on the altar of the incense for all the work of the most holy offerings and to atone for Yisroel, according to all that Moshe the servant of Elokim had commanded.
And these are the sons of Aharon: Elazar his son, Pinchas his son, Abishua his son.
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerachyah his son.
Meraioth his son, Amaryah his son, Ahitub his son.
Tzadok his son, Achimaatz his son.
And these were their settlements for their palaces in their border: for the sons of Aharon, to the family of the Kehasim, for theirs was the lot.
And they gave them Chevron in the land of Yehudah and the open land around it.
And the field of the city and its villages they gave to Kalev the son of Yefuneh.
And to the sons of Aharon they gave the cities of refuge: Chevron, and Libnah and the open land around it, and Yatir, and Eshtemoa and the open land around it.
And Hillen and the open land around it, and Devir and the open land around it.
And Ashan and the open land around it, and Beis-Shemesh and the open land around it.

And from the tribe of Binyamin, Geva and the open land around it, and Alemeth and the open land around it, and Anatot and the open land around it; all their cities were thirteen cities among their families.
And to the sons of Kehath who remained from the family of the tribe: from half the tribe of Menasheh, by lot ten cities.
And to the sons of Gershom to their families; from the tribe of Yissachar, and from the tribe of Asher, and from the tribe of Naftali, and from the tribe of Menasheh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
To the sons of Merari to their families: from the tribe of Reuven, and from the tribe of Gad, and from the tribe of Zevulun, by lot twelve cities.
And the Children of Yisroel gave the Leviim the cities and their suburbs.
And they gave by lot from the tribe of the sons of Yehudah, and from the tribe of the sons of Shimon, and from the tribe of the sons of Binyamin; these cities that they called by names.
And from the families of the sons of Kehath — the cities of their border were from the tribe of Efrayim.
And they gave them the cities of refuge: Shechem and the open land around it in Mount Efrayim, and Gezer and the open land around it.
And Yokmeam and the open land around it, and Beis-Horon and the open land around it.
And Ayalon and the open land around it, and Gat-Rimmon and the open land around it.
And from half the tribe of Menasheh, Aner and the open land around it, and Bileam and the open land around it, to the family of the remaining sons of Kehath.
To the sons of Gershom, from the family of half the tribe of Menasheh, Golan in Bashan and the open land around it, and Ashtaroth and the open land around it.
And from the tribe of Yissachar, Kedesh and the open land around it, Dobrath and the open land around it.
And Ramos and the open land around it, and Anem and the open land around it.
And from the tribe of Asher, Mashal and the open land around it, and Abdon and the open land around it.
And Hukok and the open land around it, and Rehob and the open land around it.
And from the tribe of Naftali, Kedesh in Galil and the open land around it, and Hammon and the open land around it, and Kiriathaim and the open land around it.
To the sons of Merari who remained from the tribe of Zevulun, Rimmono and the open land around it, Tabor and the open land around it.
And from the other side of the Yarden of Yericho to the east of the Yarden, from the tribe of Reuven, Bezer in the desert and the open land around it, and Yachzah and the open land around it.
And Kedemoth and the open land around it, and Mephaath and the open land around it.
And from the tribe of Gad, Ramos in Gilad and the open land around it, and Mahanaim and the open land around it.
And Cheshbon and the open land around it, and Yazer and the open land around it.
And of the sons of Yissachar: Tola, and Puah, and Yashuv, and Shimron-four.

And the sons of Tola: Uzzi, and Refayah, and Yeriel, and Yachmai, and Ibsam, and Shmuel, heads of their fathers' houses; of Tola, mighty warriors to their generations; their number in Dovid's time was twenty-two thousand and six hundred.
And the sons of Uzzi: Yizrachyah, and the sons of Yizrachyah: Michoel, and Ovadyah, and Yoel, [and] Yishiyah — all five of them heads.
And with them of their generations to the house of their fathers, military troops, thirty-six thousand, for they had many wives and sons.
And their brethren of all the families of Yissachar, mighty warriors-eighty-seven thousand, all having genealogical records.
Binyamin: Bela, and Becher, and Yediel-three.
And the sons of Bela: Ezbon, and Uzzi, and Uzziel, and Yerimos, and Iri-five heads of the father's house, mighty warriors, and their genealogical records, twenty-two thousand and thirty-four.
And the sons of Becher: Zemirah, and Yoash, and Eliezer, and Elioenai, and Omri, and Yeremos, and Aviyah, and Anatot, and Alameth — all these were the sons of Becher.
And their genealogical records to their generations, the heads of their fathers' house, mighty warriors - twenty thousand and two hundred.
And the sons of Yediel: Bilhan, and the sons of Bilhan: Jeush, and Binyamin, and Ehud, and Chenaanah, and Zethan, and Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these were the sons of Yediel: of the heads of the fathers, mighty warriors-seventeen thousand and two hundred, who go out to the army for war.
And Shupim and Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim the sons of Aher.
The sons of Naftali: Yachziel, and Guni, and Yetzer, and Shalum, the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Menasheh: Asriel, whom she bore; his Arami concubine bore Machir, the father of Gilad.
And Machir took a wife of Huppim and of Shupim, and the name of his sister was Maacah, and the name of the second was Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.
And Maacah the wife of Gilad bore a son, and she named him Peresh, and his brother's name was Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rekem.
And the sons of Ulam: Bedan. These are the sons of Gilad the son of Machir, the son of Menasheh.
And his sister who reigned bore Ishhod, and Abiezer, and Mahlah.
And the sons of Shemida: Ahian, and Shechem, and Likhi, and Aniam.
And the sons of Efrayim: Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eladah his son, and Tahath his son.
And Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer, and Elad, and the men of Gat, the natives of the land, slew them because they came down to take their cattle.
And Efrayim their father mourned for them many days, and his brothers came to console him.
And he went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and he named him Beriah, because during a time of trouble she was in his house.
And his daughter was Sheerah, and she built the lower Beis-Horon and the upper one, and Uzen Sheerah.
And Rephah was his son, and Resheph and Telah his son, and Tahan his son.
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son.
Nun his son, Yehoshua his son.
And their inheritance and their settlements were Beis El and its villages, and to the east Naaran, and to the west Gezer and its villages, and Shechem and its villages, until Aiah and its villages.
And alongside the sons of Menasheh were: Beis-Shean and its villages, Taanach and its villages, Megiddo and its villages, Dor and its villages; in these the sons of Yosef the son of Yisroel dwelt.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, and Ishvah, and Ishvi, and Beriah, and Serah their sister.
And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel; he was the father of Birzaith.
And Heber begot Yaflet, and Shomer, and Hotham, and Shua their sister.
And the sons of Yaflet: Pasach, and Bimhal, and Ashvath; these were the sons of Yaflet.
And the sons of Shemer the brother of Werogah, and Hubbah, and Aram.
And the son of Helem his brother: Zophah, and Imna, and Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, and Harnepher, and Shual, and Beri, and Imrah.
Bezer, and Hod, and Shamma, and Shilshah, and Ithran, and Beera.
And the sons of Yeser: Yefuneh, and Pispah, and Ara.
And the sons of Ulla: Ara, and Hanniel, and Rizia.

All these were the sons of Asher, the chosen heads of the fathers' houses, mighty warriors, the heads of the princes, and their genealogical records in the army in war; their number was twenty-six thousand men.
And Binyamin begot Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, and Ahrah the third.
Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.
And Bela had sons: Adar, and Gera, and Abihud.
And Abishua, and Naaman, and Ahoah.
And Gera, and Shephuphan, and Huram.
And these were the sons of Ehud: these are the heads of the fathers' [houses] of the inhabitants of Geva, and they exiled them to Manahath.
And Naaman, and Achiyah, and Gera — he exiled them, and he begot Uzza and Ahihud.
And Shaharaim begot in the field of Moav since he sent them away; Hushim and Baara were his wives.
And from Hodesh his wife he begot: Yobab, and Tzivyah, and Mesha, and Malcam.
And Yeutz, and Sachyah, and Mirmah; these are his sons, the heads of the fathers' [houses].
And from Hushim he begot Abitub and Elpaal.
And the sons of Elpaal: Eiver, and Misham, and Shemed; he built Ono and Lod and its villages.
And Beriah and Shema — they were the heads of the fathers' [houses] of the inhabitants of Ayalon; they put the inhabitants of Gat to flight.
And Ahio, Shashak, and Yeremos.
And Zevadyah, and Arad, and Eder.
And Michoel, and Ishpah, and Yoha — the sons of Beriah.
And Zevadyah, and Meshullam, and Hizki, and Heber.
And Ishmerai, and Yitzliyah, and Yobab — the sons of Elpaal.
And Yakim, and Zichri, and Zabdi.
And Elienai, and Zillethai, and Eliel.
And Adayah, and Berayah, and Shimrath — the sons of Shimi.
And Ishpan, and Eiver, and Eliel.
And Abdon, and Zichri, and Chanan.
And Chananyah, and Eilam, and Antotiyah.
And Yifdeyah, and Penuel — the sons of Shashak.
And Shamsherai, and Shecharyah, and Atalyah.
And Yaareshyah, and Eliyahu, and Zichri — the sons of Yerocham.
These are the heads of the fathers' [houses] to their generations, the heads — these dwelt in Yerushalayim.
And in Givon dwelt the leader of Givon, and his wife's name was Maacah.
And his firstborn son was Abdon, and Zur, and Kish, and Baal and Nadab.
And Gedor, and Ahio, and Zecher.
And Mikloth begot Shimah, and they too, opposite their brethren, dwelt in Yerushalayim with their brethren.
And Ner begot Kish, and Kish begot Shaul, and Shaul begot Yonasan, and Malcishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
And Yonasan's son was Merib-Baal, and Merib-Baal begot Michah.
And the sons of Michah: Pithon, and Melech, and Tarea, and Achaz.
And Achaz begot Yehoadah, and Yehoadah begot Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri begot Moza.
And Moza begot Binah; Raphah his son, Elasah his son, Azel his son.
And Azel had six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam his firstborn, and Yishmael, and Shearyah, and Ovadyah, and Chanan — all these were the sons of Azel.
And the sons of Ashek, his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
And the sons of Ulam were mighty warriors who draw the bow, with many children and grandchildren, one hundred and fifty — all these were the sons of Binyamin.
And all Yisroel traced their genealogy, and behold they are written in the book of the kings of Yisroel; but the Yehudim were exiled to Bavel because of their treachery.
And the first settlers who were in their inheritance in their cities were the Yisroelim, the priests, the Leviim, and the Nethinim.
But in Yerushalayim there dwelt some of the sons of Yehudah and some of the sons of Binyamin, and some of the sons of Efrayim and Menasheh.
Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the sons of Peretz the son of Yehudah.
And of the Shilonim: Asayah the firstborn and his sons.
And of the sons of Zerah: Yeuel and their brethren-six hundred and ninety.
And of the sons of Binyamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodavyah, the son of Hassenuah.
And Yivneyah the son of Yerocham and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shefatyah, the son of Reuel, the son of Yivneyah.
And their brethren according to their generations-nine hundred and fifty-six; all these were prominent men, the heads of fathers' [houses] by the house of their fathers.
And of the priests: Yedayah, and Yehoyariv, and Yachin.
And Azaryah the son of Chilkiyah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Tzadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, ruler of the House of Elokim.
And Adayah the son of Yerocham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malkiyah, and Maasai the son of Adiel, the son of Yachzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer.
And their brethren, heads of the house of their fathers — a thousand, seven hundred and sixty mighty warriors, [appointed over] the work of the service of the House of Elokim.
And of the Leviim: Shemayah the son of Hashub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Chashavyah, of the sons of Merari.
And Bakbakkar, Heresh, and Galal, and Matanyah the son of Micha, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaf.
And Ovadyah the son of Shemayah, the son of Galal, the son of Yedusun, and Berechyah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who dwelt in the towns of the Netofasim.
And the gate sentries: Shalum, and Akkub, and Talmon, and Ahiman, and their brethren; Shalum was the head.
And from here until the king's gate to the east, they are the gate sentries of the camps of the sons of Levi.

And Shalum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korach, and his brethren of his father's house, the Korchim, over the work of the service, the guards of the thresholds of the Tent, and their fathers over the camp of Havayah, the guards of the entry.
And Pinchas the son of Elazar was the ruler over them in time past, Havayah being with him.
Zecharyah the son of Meshelemyah, the gate sentry of the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
They were all the chosen to be gate sentries in the thresholds-two hundred and twelve; they were reckoned by genealogy in their villages, whom Dovid and Shmuel the seer established permanently.
And they and their sons were in charge of the gates of the House of Havayah, of the House of the Tent according to watches.
At the four corners were the gate sentries: east, west, north, and south.
And their brethren in their towns [were required] to come for seven days from time to time with these.
For they were permanently four mighty gate sentries — they are the Leviim, and they were in charge of the chambers and the treasuries of the House of Elokim.
And around the House of Elokim they would lodge, for the watch was incumbent upon them, and they were [appointed] over the key[s] and [to open the gates] every morning.
And some of them were in charge of the service vessels, for they would bring them in by number and take them out by number.
And some of them were appointed over the vessels and over all the vessels of the Sanctuary and over the fine flour, and the wine, and the oil, and the frankincense, and the spices.
And some of the sons of the priests were compounders of the mixture for the spices.
And Matisyah of the Leviim — he was the firstborn of Shalum the Korchi — was entrusted with the making of the pancakes.
And some of the sons of the Kehasim, of their brethren, were in charge of the showbread to prepare every Sabbath.
And these are the singers, the heads of the fathers' [houses] of the Leviim in the chambers, who were exempt, for day and night it is incumbent upon them [to engage] in the work.
These are the heads of the fathers' [houses] of the Leviim, over their generations, they were heads; these dwelt in Yerushalayim.
And in Givon dwelt the leader of Givon, Yeiel, whose wife's name was Maacah.
And his firstborn son was Abdon, and Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Ner, and Nadab.
And Gedor, and Ahio, and Zecharyah, and Mikloth.
And Mikloth begot Shimeam, and they too opposite their brethren dwelt in Yerushalayim with their brethren.
And Ner begot Kish, and Kish begot Shaul, and Shaul begot Yonasan, and Malchi-shua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
And the son of Yonasan was Merib-Baal, and Meri-Baal begot Michah.
And the sons of Michah: Pithon, and Melech, and Tahrea.
And Achaz begot Yaarah, and Yaarah begot Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri begot Moza.
And Moza begot Binea and Refayah his son, Elasah his son, Azel his son.
And Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam and Bochru and Yishmael, and Shearyah and Ovadyah and Chanan; these are the sons of Azel.
And the Pelishtim fought with Yisroel, and the men of Yisroel fled from before the Pelishtim, and they fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
And the Pelishtim pursued closely after Shaul and his sons, and the Pelishtim smote Yonasan, and Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Shaul.
And the battle bore heavily on Shaul, and the archers discovered him, and he was terrified of the archers.

And Shaul said to his weapon-bearer, "Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised ones come upon me and make a mockery of me," but his weapon-bearer was unwilling, for he feared greatly, and Shaul took the sword and fell upon it.
And his weapon-bearer saw that Shaul had died, and he too fell upon the sword and died.
And Shaul and his three sons died, and his entire household together died.
And all the men of Yisroel who were in the valley saw that they fled and that Shaul and his sons died, and they abandoned their cities and fled, and the Pelishtim came and settled in them.
And it came about on the morrow that the Pelishtim came to strip the slain, and they found Shaul and his sons lying on Mount Gilboa.
And they stripped him and carried off his head and his weapons, and they sent throughout the land of Pelishtim all around to bring the news to the priests of their idols and to the people.
And they deposited his weapons in the temple of their gods, and his skull they impaled in the temple of Dagon.
And all of Yaveish-Gilad heard all that the Pelishtim had done to Shaul.
And all the valiant men arose and carried off Shaul's body and the bodies of his sons and brought them to Yaveish, and they buried their bones beneath the oak in Yaveish, and they fasted seven days.
And Shaul died because of the treachery that he had committed against Havayah, concerning the word of Havayah that he did not keep, and also because he had inquired of the dead spirit.
And he did not inquire of Havayah, and He slew him, and transferred the kingdom to Dovid the son of Yishai.
And all Yisroel gathered to Dovid to Chevron, saying, "Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.

Also in times past, also when Shaul was king, you were the one who led Yisroel out and brought [them in], and Havayah your Elokim said to you, 'You shall shepherd My people Yisroel, and you shall be a ruler over My people Yisroel.'

And all the elders of Yisroel came to the king to Chevron, and Dovid made with them a covenant in Chevron before Havayah, and they anointed Dovid as king over Yisroel, according to the word of Havayah by the hand of Shmuel.
And Dovid and all of Yisroel went to Yerushalayim, that is Yevus, and there were the Yevusim, the inhabitants of the land.
And the inhabitants of Yevus said to Dovid, "You shall not come here," and Dovid captured the citadel of Tziyon, that is the City of Dovid.
And Dovid said, "Whoever smites the Yevusim first will be a chief and an officer," and Yoav the son of Zeruyah ascended first and became a chief.
And Dovid dwelt in the citadel; therefore they called it the City of Dovid.
And he built the city from around, from the Millo until the surrounding area, and Yoav restored the rest of the city.
And Dovid waxed constantly greater, and Havayah of Hosts was with him.
And these are the chiefs of Dovid's mighty men who held strongly with him in his kingdom with all Yisroel to crown him-according to the word of Havayah concerning Yisroel.
And these are the number of Dovid's mighty men: Yashovam the son of Hachmoni, the head of the mighty men; he stirred his spear on three hundred slain at one time.
And after him was Elazar the son of Dodo the Achochi; he was among the three mighty men.
He was with Dovid in Pas-Dammim, and the Pelishtim gathered there for war, and the plot of ground was full of barley, and the people fled from before the Pelishtim.
And they stationed themselves in the midst of the plot and saved it and smote the Pelishtim, and Havayah performed a great salvation.
And three of the thirty descended upon the rock to Dovid, to the cave of Adulam, and the Pelishti camp was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
Now Dovid was then in the stronghold, and a Pelishti governor was then in Beis Lechem.
And Dovid experienced a craving and said, "If only someone would give me to drink water from the cistern of Beis Lechem, which is by the gate!"

And the three broke through the Pelishti camp, drew water from the cistern of Beis Lechem, which is by the gate, carried and brought [it] to Dovid, but he was unwilling to drink it, and he poured it out as a libation to Havayah.

And he said, "Far be it from me from my Elokim from doing this; shall I drink the blood of these men who went in jeopardy of their lives, for they brought it with their lives," and he was unwilling to drink it. The three mighty men performed these [feats].
And Abshai, the brother of Yoav was the chief of the three, and he lifted his spear on three hundred slain, and he had a name among the three.
Of the three, he was honored like two, and he was their chief, but to the three he did not come.
Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, a valiant man, who accomplished many feats, from Kabzeel — he smote the two mighty men of Moav, and he descended and smote the lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day.

And he smote a Mitzri man, a man of great stature of five cubits, and in the Mitzri's hand was a spear like a weavers' beam, and he went down to him with a rod, and he robbed the Mitzri of the spear and slew him with his spear.
Benayahu the son of Yehoyada performed these [feats], and he had a name among the three mighty men.
Of the thirty, he was the most honored, but to the three he did not come, and Dovid appointed him over his guard.
And the mighty warriors were: Asahel the brother of Yoav, Elchanan the son of Dodo of Beis Lechem.
Shammoth the Harori, Helez the Paloni.
Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoi, Abiezer the Anatoti.
Sibbecai the Chushasi, Ilai the Achochi.
Mahrai the Netofasi, Heled the son of Baanah the Netofasi.
Ithai the son of Ribai, of Givah of the sons of Binyamin, Benayahu the Pirasoni.
Hurai of Nahalei Gaash, Abiel the Arvasi.
Azmaveth the Bacharumi, Eljahba the Shaalboni.
The sons of Hashem the Gizzoni, Yonasan the son of Shageh the Harari.
Ahiam the son of Sachar the Harari, Eliphal the son of Ur.
Hepher the Mecherasi, Achiyah the Paloni.
Hezro the Carmeli, Naarai the son of Ezbai.
Yoel the brother of Nasan, Mibhar the son of Hagri.
Zelek the Ammoni, Nahrai the Beirosi, the weapon-bearer of Yoav the son of Zeruyah.
Ira the Yisri, Gareb the Yisri.
Uriyah the Chiti, Zabad the son of Ahlai.
Adina the son of Shiza the Reubeni, the head of the Reuvenim, and with him [were] thirty [men].
Chanan the son of Maacah and Yehoshafat the Misni.
Uzzia the Ashterasi, Shama, and Yeiel, the sons of Hotham the Aroeri.
Yediel the son of Shimri and Yoha his brother, the Titzis.
Eliel the Machavi, and Yerivai, and Yoshavyah the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moavi.
Eliel, and Obed, and Yaasiel the Metzovai.
And these are the ones who came to Dovid to Tziklag, while he was still hiding from Shaul the son of Kish, and they were among the mighty men who aided the war.
Armed with bows, shooting with the right and left hands, with stones and with arrows in the bow, of Shaul's brethren of Binyamin.
The chief, Ahiezer, and Yoash, the sons of Hashemaah the Givasi, and Yeziel, and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth and Berachah, and Yehu the Anatoti.
And Yishmayah the Givoni, the mightiest of the thirty and over the thirty.
And Yirmeyah, and Yahaziel, and Yochanan, and Yozabad the Gederasi, Eleuzai, and Yerimos, and Bealyah, and Shemaryah, and Shefatyah the Charufi.
Elkanah, and Yishiyah, and Azarel, and Yoezer, and Yashovam, the Korchim.
And Yoelah, and Zevadyah, the sons of Yerocham of Gedud.

And some of the Gadim were separated to Dovid to the stronghold of the desert, valiant warriors, soldiers for battle, who could handle shield and spear, and whose faces were [like] the faces of lions, and as swift as gazelles on the mountains.
Ezer the chief, Ovadyah the second, Eliab the third.
Mishmannah the fourth, Yirmeyah the fifth.
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh.
Yochanan the eighth, Elzavad the ninth.
Yirmeyah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.
These were some of the sons of Gad, the heads of the army; the smallest one [could pursue] a hundred, and the greatest a thousand.
These are the ones who crossed the Yarden in the first month, when it was overflowing all its banks, and they put all the valley-dwellers to flight to the east and to the west.
And there came some of the sons of Binyamin and Yehudah up to the stronghold to Dovid.

And Dovid came out before them, and he answered and said to them, "If you have come to me in peace to help me, my heart will be upon you as one, but if you have come to betray me to my adversaries although there is no injustice in my hands, may the Elokim of our forefathers see and reprove."

And a spirit enwrapped Amasai, the chief of the the officers, "To you, Dovid, and with you, O son of Yishai; peace, peace to you and peace to your helper, for your Elokim has helped you." And Dovid received them and placed them at the head of the troop.

And from Menasheh there defected to Dovid when he came with the Pelishtim against Shaul in battle, but they did not help them, for with a counsel the chiefs of the Pelishtim sent him away, saying, "With [jeopardy to] our heads he will defect to his master, Shaul."
When he went to Tziklag, [some men] of Menasheh defected to him; namely Adnah, and Yozabad, and Yediel, and Michoel, and Yozabad, and Elihu, and Zillethai, chiefs of the thousands of Menasheh.
And they helped Dovid against the troop, for they were all mighty warriors, and they became officers in the army.
For from day to day, [men] came to Dovid to help him, until it became a huge camp, like the camp of Elokim.
And these are the numbers of the chiefs of the armed men of the army [who] came to Dovid to Chevron to turn Shaul's kingdom to him, according to Havayah's decree.
The sons of Yehudah, bearing shield and spear, six thousand and eight hundred armed men of the army.
Of the sons of Shimon, mighty warriors for the army-seven thousand and one hundred.
Of the sons of the Leviim-four thousand and six hundred.
And Yehoyada was the ruler of Aharon, and with him were three thousand and seven hundred.
And Tzadok was a youth, a mighty warrior, and his father's house had twenty-two offfcers.
And of the sons of Binyamin, Shaul's brethren, were three thousand, and heretofore their majority had kept the watch of the house of Shaul.
And of the sons of Efrayim-twenty thousand and eight hundred, mighty warriors, famous men of their fathers' houses.
And of half the tribe of Menasheh-eighteen thousand who were designated by names to come and to crown Dovid.
And of the sons of Yissachar, those who had an understanding of the times, to know what Yisroel should do; their chiefs were two hundred, and all their brethren obeyed their word.
Of Zevulun, those going out in the army with all sorts of weapons-fifty thousand, and who could wage war and were not of double heart.
And of Naftali — a thousand officers, and with them with shield and spear-thirty-seven thousand.
And of the Danim, who set up the battle array-twenty-eight thousand and six hundred.
And of Asher, those going out in the army to wage war-forty thousand.
And from across the Yarden, of the Reuvenim and the Gadim and half the tribe of Menasheh, with all sorts of weapons — a hundred and twenty thousand.
All these were men of war, setting up the battle array; wholeheartedly they came to Chevron to crown Dovid over all Yisroel, and also the entire remnant of Yisroel was of one heart to crown Dovid.
And they were there with Dovid for three days, eating and drinking, for their brethren had made preparations for them.

And also those near to them, until Yissachar and Zevulun and Naftali were bringing food on donkeys, and on camels, and on mules, and on cattle, food made of flour, dried figs, and raisins, and wine, and oil, and cattle, and sheep in abundance, for there was joy in Yisroel.
And Dovid conferred with the officers of the thousands and the hundreds, with every leader.

And Dovid said to the entire congregation of Yisroel, "If it pleases you, and from Havayah our Elokim, it has been opened, let us send to our brethren remaining in all the lands of Yisroel, and with them, the priests and the Leviim in the cities of their open land, and let them gather to us.
And let us bring the Ark of our Elokim around to us, for we did not seek Him in the days of Shaul."
And all the congregation said to do so, because the matter was deemed proper by the whole nation.
And Dovid assembled all Yisroel from Shihor of Mitzrayim and until the approach to Hamath, to bring the Ark of Elokim from Kiryas-Yearim.
And Dovid and all Yisroel went up to Baalah, to Kiryas-Yearim of Yehudah, to bring up from there the Ark of Elokim Havayah, Who dwells between the cherubim, upon which the Name is called.
And they set the Ark of Elokim on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, and Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.
And Dovid and all Yisroel made merry before Elokim with all [their] might, and with songs, and with harps, and with psalteries, and with timbrels, and with cymbals, and with trumpets.
And they came to Goren Kidon, and Uzza stretched forth his hand to take hold of the Ark because the oxen stumbled.
And the anger of Havayah was kindled against Uzza, and He struck him down because he stretched forth his hand upon the Ark, and he died there before Elokim.
And Dovid was angered, because Havayah had made a breach upon Uzza, and he called that place Peretz-Uzza until this very day.
And Dovid feared Elokim on that day, saying, "How will I bring the Ark of Elokim to me?"
And Dovid did not remove the Ark to himself to the City of Dovid, but he set it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gitti.
And the Ark of Elokim stayed at the house of Obed-Edom three months, and Havayah blessed the house of Obed-Edom and all that was his.
And Hiram the king of Tzor sent emissaries to Dovid and cedar wood and masons and carpenters to build him a house.
And Dovid knew that Havayah had established him as king over Yisroel, because his kingdom had been exalted highly for the sake of His people Yisroel.
And Dovid took more wives in Yerushalayim, and Dovid begot more sons and daughters.
And these are the names of those born whom he had in Yerushalayim: Shamua, and Shovav, Nasan, and Shlomo.
And Ibhar, and Elishua, and Elpelet.
And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Yafia.
And Elishama, and Beeljada, and Eliphelet.
And the Pelishtim heard that Dovid had been anointed as king over all Yisroel, and all the Pelishtim went up to seek Dovid, and Dovid heard and went out before them.
And the Pelishtim came and spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
And Dovid inquired of Elokim, saying, "Shall I go up against the Pelishtim, and will You deliver them into my hand?" And Havayah said to him, "Go up, and I shall deliver them into your hand."
And they went up to Baal-Perazim, and Dovid smote them there, and Dovid said, "Elokim has broken my enemies in my hand like a breach of waters." Therefore, they named that place Baal-Perazim.
And they abandoned their deities there, and Dovid commanded, and they were burnt with fire.
And the Pelishtim continued further and spread out in the valley.
And Dovid inquired again of Elokim, and Elokim said to him, "You shall not go up after them; circle them, and you shall come to them opposite the mulberry trees.
And it will be when you hear the sound of steps in the tops of the mulberry trees, then you shall go forth in the battle, because Elokim has gone forth before you to smite the camp of the Pelishtim."
And Dovid did as Elokim had commanded him, and they smote the camp of the Pelishtim from Givon until Gazerah.
And Dovid's fame went forth throughout all the lands, and Havayah placed the fear of him upon all the nations.
And [Dovid] made himself houses in the City of Dovid, and he prepared a place for the Ark of Elokim, and he pitched a tent for it.
Then Dovid said, "It is not proper to carry the Ark of Elokim except the Leviim, for Havayah chose them to carry the Ark of Elokim and to serve Him forever."
And Dovid congregated all Yisroel to Yerushalayim, to bring up the Ark of Havayah to its place, which he had prepared for it.
And Dovid gathered the sons of Aharon and the Leviim.
Of the sons of Kehath: Uriel the leader, and his brethren a hundred and twenty.
Of the sons of Merari: Asayah the leader, and his brethren two hundred and twenty.
Of the sons of Gershom: Yoel the leader, and his brethren a hundred and thirty.
Of the sons of Elitzafan: Shemayah the leader, and his brethren two hundred.
Of the sons of Chevron: Eliel the leader, and his brethren eighty.
Of the sons of Uzziel: Amminadab the leader, and his brethren a hundred and twelve.
And Dovid summoned Tzadok and Ebiathar the priests, and of the Leviim, Uriel, Asayah and Yoel, Shemayah and Eliel and Amminadab.

And he said to them, "You are the heads of the fathers' [houses] of the Leviim; prepare yourselves and your brethren, and you shall bring up the Ark of Havayah Elokim of Yisroel to [the place] I have prepared for it.
For from the beginning, [when] you were not [the bearers], Havayah, our Elokim, made a breach in us, for we did not seek Him according to the ordinance."
And the priests and the Leviim prepared themselves to bring up the Ark of Havayah Elokim of Yisroel.
And the sons of the Leviim carried the Ark of Elokim as Moshe had commanded according to the word of Havayah, on their shoulders, with staves upon them.
And Dovid said to the leaders of the Leviim to station their brethren, the singers, with musical instruments, psalteries and harps and cymbals, resounding to raise a voice in joy.
And the Leviim stationed Heiman the son of Yoel and of his brethren, Asaf the son of Berechyah, and of the sons of Merari their brethren, Eitan the son of Kushayah.

And with them, their brethren the second in rank; Zecharyah Ben and Yaaziel and Shemiramos and Yechiel and Unni and Eliab and Benayahu and Maaseyah and Matisyah and Eliphelehu and Mikneyah and Obed-Edom and Yeiel the door sentries.
And the singers: Heiman, Asaf, and Eitan, with copper cymbals to resound.
And Zecharyah and Aziel and Shemiramos and Yeiel and Unni and Eliab and Maaseyah and Benayahu with psalteries over alamoth.
And Matisyah and Eliphelehu and Mikneyah and Obed-Edom and Yeiel and Azazyah, with harps on the sheminith, to conduct.
And Kenanyah, the leader of the Leviim in song; he would chastise in song because he was an expert.
And Berechyah and Elkanah were gate sentries for the Ark.

And Shevanyah and Yehoshafat and Nethanel and Amasai and Zecharyah and Benayahu and Eliezer, the priests, sounding the trumpets before the Ark of Elokim, and Obed-Edom and Yechiyah were gate sentries for the Ark.
And Dovid and the elders of Yisroel and the leaders of the thousands who went to bring up the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah from the House of Obed-Edom were rejoicing.
And it came to pass when Elokim helped the Leviim, the bearers of the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah, that they slaughtered seven bulls and seven rams.
And Dovid was enwrapped in a linen robe, and all the Leviim who were carrying the Ark, and the singers and Kenanyah the leader of the singers in the song, and on Dovid was a linen ephod.
And all Yisroel were bringing up the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah, with the sounds and blasts of the shofar and with trumpets and with cymbals, resounding with psalteries and harps.

And the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah came up to the City of Dovid, and Michal the daughter of Shaul peered through the window, and she saw King Dovid dancing and playing, and she scorned him in her heart.
And they brought the Ark of Elokim, and they set it up in the midst of the tent that Dovid had pitched for it, and they offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before Elokim.
And Dovid finished offering up the burnt-offering[s] and the peace-offerings, and he blessed the people in the Name of Havayah.
And he distributed to every person of Yisroel, both to men and women, to each individual a loaf of bread and a portion of meat and a flask of wine.
And he stationed before the Ark of Havayah some of the ministering Leviim, and to make mention and to give thanks and to praise Havayah Elokim of Yisroel.

Asaf the leader and second to him Zecharyah, Yeiel and Shemiramos and Yechiel and Matisyah and Eliab and Benayahu and Obed-Edom and Yeiel, with instruments of psalteries and with harps, and Asaf was resounding with the cymbals.
And Benayahu and Yahaziel the priests with trumpets constantly, were before the Ark of the Covenant of Elokim.
On that day, Dovid ordained to give thanks to Havayah by the hand of Asaf and his brethren.
"Give thanks to Havayah, call out in His Name; make His exploits known among the peoples.
Sing to Him, play music to Him, speak of all His wonders.
Glory in His holy Name; may the heart of those who seek Havayah rejoice.
Search for Havayah and His might; seek His presence constantly.
Remember His wonders, which He performed, His miracles and the judgments of His mouth.
The seed of Yisroel His servant, the children of Yackov, His chosen ones.
He is Havayah our Elokim; throughout the earth are His judgments.
Remember His covenant forever, the word which He commanded to a thousand generations.
[The covenant] which He had made with Avraham, and His oath to Yitzchak.
And He set it up for Yackov as a statute, to Yisroel as an everlasting covenant.
Saying: To you I shall give the land of Kena'an, the lot of your inheritance."
When you were few in number, hardly dwelling in it.
And when they walked from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people.
He let no man oppress them, and He reproved kings on their account;
"Do not touch My anointed ones, and do not harm My prophets."
Sing to Havayah, all the earth; announce His salvation from day to day.
Tell of His glory among the nations, among all peoples His wonders.
For Havayah is great and very much praised; He is feared over all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but Havayah made the heavens.
There is beauty and majesty before Him; might and joy in His place.
Ascribe to Havayah, [you] families of peoples, ascribe to Havayah glory and might.
Ascribe to Havayah the glory of His name; carry an offering and come before Him; bow down to Havayah in the beauty of holiness.
Quake before Him, all the earth; also the inhabited world will be established so that it will not falter.
The heavens will rejoice and the earth will exult, and they will say among the nations, "Havayah has reigned."
The sea and the fullness thereof will roar. The field and all that is therein will jubilate.
Then all the forest trees will sing praises, before Havayah, for He has come to judge the earth.
Give thanks to Havayah for He is good, for His loving-kindness exists forever.
And say, "Save us, O Elokim of our salvation, and gather us and save us from the nations, to give thanks to Your holy Name, to triumph in your praise."
Blessed is Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel from all times past, and to all times to come." And all the people said, "Amen," and praised Havayah.
And he left before the Ark of Havayah Asaf and his brethren to serve before the Ark continually as every day's work required.
And Obed-Edom and his brethren [were] sixty-eight, and Obed-Edom the son of Yedusun and Hosah for gate sentries.
And Tzadok the priest and his brethren the priests were before the Tabernacle of Havayah in the high place that was in Givon.

To offer up burnt offerings to Havayah upon the altar of the burnt offering constantly in the morning and in the evening, and for all that is written in the Law of Havayah, which He commanded upon Yisroel.
And with them were Heiman and Yedusun and the rest of the chosen ones who were designated with names, to give thanks to Havayah, for His loving-kindness exists forever.
And with them, Heiman and Yedusun, were trumpets and cymbals for resounding, and instruments of the song of Elokim, and the sons of Yedusun were [appointed] over the gate.
And all the people went, each one to his house, and Dovid returned to bless his household.
Now it came to pass when Dovid sat in his house, that Dovid said to Nasan the prophet, "Behold, I dwell in a house of the cedars, but the Ark of Havayah dwells under curtains."
And Nasan said to Dovid, "All that is in your heart do, for Elokim is with you."
And it came to pass on that same night, that the word of Elokim came to Nasan, saying,
"Go and say to Dovid, My servant: So Havayah said, 'You shall not build me the house [in which] to dwell.
For I have not dwelt in a house from the day that I brought up Yisroel, to this day, but I have [gone] from tent to tent and from tabernacle [to another].
Wherever I walked among all Yisroel, I spoke a word with any of the judges of Yisroel, whom I commanded to shepherd My people, saying: Why have you not built for Me a house of cedar?
And now, so shall you say to My servant, to Dovid: So Havayah of Hosts said; I took you from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be a leader over My people, Yisroel.
And I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you, and I made you a name, like the name of the great ones that are in the Earth.
And I shall appoint a place for My people Yisroel, and I shall plant them, and they will dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more, and wicked people will no longer afflict them as formerly.
And even from the days that I commanded judges over My people Yisroel; and I vanquished all your enemies. Moreover I tell you that Havayah will build you a house.
And it will come to pass when your days are finished to go with your forefathers, then I shall raise up your seed after you, who will be of your sons, and I shall establish his kingdom.
He will build Me a house, and I shall establish his throne forever.
I shall be to him as a father, and he will be to Me as a son, and I shall not remove My loving-kindness from him as I removed [it] from he who was before you.
And I shall station him in My house and in My kingdom forever, and his throne shall be established forever."
According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nasan speak to Dovid.
And King Dovid came and sat before Havayah, and he said, "Who am I, O Havayah Elokim, and who is my house, that You have brought me thus far?
As though this was yet too small a thing in Your eyes, O Elokim, but You also spoke of Your servant from afar, and You have regarded me in the manner of a man of high degree, O Havayah Elokim.
What more need Dovid [seek] You, to have glory as Your servant? For You know Your servant.
O Havayah, for the sake of Your servant, and according to Your heart, You have brought about all this greatness, to make Your servant know all the great things.
O Havayah, there is none like You, and there is no Elokim besides You according to all that we have heard with our ears.

And who is like Your people Yisroel, one nation in the world, whom Elokim went to redeem for Himself [as] a people, to make You a name of great and fearful things, to drive nations from before Your people, whom You redeemed from Mitzrayim.
And You made Your people Yisroel [to be] to You as a people forever, and You, O Havayah, became their Elokim.
And now, O Havayah, the word that You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house shall be realized forever, and do as You have spoken.
And may Your name be confirmed and magnified forever, saying: Havayah of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisroel, is Elokim to Yisroel, and the house of Dovid Your servant shall be established before You.
For You, my Elokim have revealed to Your servant's ear, to build him a house; therefore, Your servant has found [occasion] to pray before You.
And now, O Havayah, You are Elokim, and You have spoken concerning Your servant this good thing.
And now, You have commenced to bless Your servant's house to be before You forever, for You, O Havayah, have blessed, and [he shall be] blessed forever."
And it came to pass afterwards that Dovid smote the Pelishtim and vanquished them, and he took Gat and its villages from the hand[s] of the Pelishtim.
And he smote Moav, and the Moavim became vassals to Dovid, paying tribute.
And Dovid smote Hadadezer, king of Zobah, in Hamath, when he went to establish his power in the Peras River.
And Dovid captured from him a thousand chariots and seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand footmen; and Dovid hamstrung all the chariot [horses] and left over of them a hundred chariots.
And Aram of Damesek came to aid Hadadezer, king of Zobah, and Dovid smote of Aram twenty-two thousand men.
And Dovid placed [garrisons] in Aram of Damesek, and the Aramim became vassals to Dovid, paying tribute, and Havayah gave victory to Dovid wherever he went.
And Dovid took the golden quivers that were on Hadadezer's servants and brought them to Yerushalayim.
And from Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadadezer, Dovid took huge quantities of copper, from which Shlomo made the copper sea and the pillars and the copper vessels.
And Tou, the king of Hamath, heard that Dovid had defeated all the army of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah.

And he sent Hadoram, his son, to King Dovid to greet him and to bless him because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him, for Hadadezer had been Tou's opponent in war, and [he had with him] all vessels of gold, of silver, and of copper.

Those also King Dovid dedicated to Havayah, [along] with the silver and the gold that he took from all the nations; from Edom and from Moav and from the children of Ammon and from the Pelishtim and from Amalek.
And Abshai the son of Zeruyah smote the Edomim in the Valley of Salt, eighteen thousand.
And he placed governors in Edom, and all the Edomim were vassals to Dovid, and Havayah made Dovid victorious wherever he went.
And Dovid reigned over all Yisroel, and he administered justice and charity for all his people.
Now Yoav the son of Zeruyah was over the host, and Yehoshafat the son of Ahilud was recorder.
And Tzadok the son of Ahitub and Avimelech the son of Ebiathar were priests, and Shavsha was scribe.
And Benayahu the son of Yehoyada was over the Kereisi and the Pelesim, and the sons of Dovid were first at the king's hand.
And it came to pass after this, that Nahash the king of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his stead.

And Dovid said, "I shall show kindness to Chanun the son of Nahash, because his father showed me kindness." And Dovid sent emissaries to comfort him concerning his father, and Dovid's servants came to the land of the children of Ammon, to Chanun to comfort him.

And the princes of the children of Ammon said to Chanun, "Do you think that Dovid honors your father because he sent you comforters? Is it not in order to investigate and to search and to spy out the land that his servants have come to you?"
And Chanun took Dovid's servants, and he shaved them, and he cut their garments in half up to their groin and he sent them away.

And they went and told Dovid about the men, and he sent [people] to meet them, for the men were very much ashamed. And the king said, "Remain in Yericho until your beards grow, and [then] you shall return. "

And the children of Ammon saw that they had become odious to Dovid, and Chanun and the children of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and riders from Aram-Naharaim and from Aram-Maacah and from Zobah.

And they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots and the king of Maacah and his people, and they came and encamped before Medeba, and the children of Ammon gathered from their cities and came to war.
And Dovid heard [of it], and he sent Yoav and the entire host of the mighty warriors.
And the children of Ammon came out, and they prepared the battle at the entrance of the city, and the kings who had come were by themselves in the field.
And Yoav saw that the battle front was before and behind him, and he chose of all the choice men of Yisroel, and he put [them] in array against the Aramim.
And the rest of the people he gave into the hands of Abshai his brother, and they put themselves in array against the children of Ammon.
And he said, "If the Aramim will be too strong for me, then you shall be my aid, and if the children of Ammon will be too strong for you, then I shall aid you.
Be strong, and let us strengthen ourselves on behalf of our people and on behalf of the cities of our Elokim, and may Havayah do what is good in His eyes."
And Yoav and the people that were with him drew forward to do battle against the Aramim, and they fled before him.
And [when] the children of Ammon saw that the Aramim had fled, they too fled from before Abshai his brother, and they came to the city, and Yoav came to Yerushalayim.

And the Aramim saw that they were smitten before Yisroel, and they sent emissaries and brought out the Aramim who were on the other side of the river and Shophach the general of the army of Hadadezer was before them.

And it was told to Dovid, and he gathered together all Yisroel, and he crossed the Yarden and came to them, and set himself against them, and Dovid set himself in battle array against the Aramim, and they fought with him.
And the Aramim fled from before Yisroel, and Dovid slew of the Aramim [the men of] seven thousand chariots and forty thousand foot soldiers, and he put Shophach the general to death.
And the servants of Hadadezer saw that they were smitten before Yisroel, and they made peace with Dovid and served him, and Aram no longer wished to aid the children of Ammon.

Now it came to pass at the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out to battle, that Yoav led the power of the army and destroyed the land of the children of Ammon, and he came and besieged Rabbah, and Dovid was dwelling in Yerushalayim, and Yoav smote Rabbah and destroyed it.

And Dovid took the crown of Malkam off his head, and he found it to weigh a talent of gold, and in it was a precious stone, and it was set on Dovid's head, and the spoils of the city he took out in large quantity.

And the people who were in it he brought forth and sawed with a saw and with harrows of iron and with saws, and so did Dovid do to all the cities of the children of Ammon, and Dovid and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.
Now it came to pass after this that a war arose in Gezer with the Pelishtim; then Sibbecai the Chushasi smote Sippai of the sons of Rapha, and they were vanquished.
And there was another war with the Pelishtim, and Elchanan the son of Yair smote Lahmi the brother of Golyas the Gitti, and the staff of his spear was as [thick as] a weavers' beam.
And there was another war in Gat, and there was a man of great stature, and his fingers were six and six, totaling twenty-four, and he too was born to Raphah.
And he taunted Yisroel, and Yonasan the son of Shimea, Dovid's brother, smote him.
These were born to Raphah in Gat, and they fell by the hand of Dovid and by the hand of his servants.
Now Satan arose upon Yisroel, and he moved Dovid to count Yisroel.
And Dovid said to Yoav and to the princes of the people, "Go count Yisroel from Be'er Sheva until Dan, and bring me [word], so that I may know their number."

And Yoav replied, "May Havayah add to His people a hundredfold of whatsoever they may be. My master, the king, are they not all servants to my master? Why does my master request this? Why should this become guilt for Yisroel?"
But the king's word prevailed over Yoav, and Yoav went forth and walked throughout Yisroel, and came to Yerushalayim.

And Yoav gave the number of the census of the people to Dovid, and all Yisroel were a thousand thousand and a hundred thousand men who draw the sword, and Yehudah was four hundred seventy thousand men who draw the sword.
But Levi and Binyamin he did not count among them because the word of the king was repugnant to Yoav.
Now Elokim was displeased because of this thing, and He smote Yisroel.
And Dovid said to Elokim, "I have sinned greatly in that I have done this thing, and now, please put aside the iniquity of Your servant, for I was very foolish."
And Havayah spoke to Gad, Dovid's seer, saying:
"Go and speak to Dovid, saying: So Havayah said: Three things I offer you; choose one of them, and I shall do it to you."
And Gad came to Dovid, and said to him, "So Havayah said; Choose which you will.

Either three years famine or three months in which you will be destroyed by your enemies, and the sword of your enemies will overtake you, or three days of the sword of Havayah and pestilence in the land, and the angel of Havayah destroying throughout the boundary of Yisroel; and now consider what I should reply to Him Who sent me."
And Dovid said to Gad, "I am greatly oppressed; let me fall now into the hand of Havayah, for His mercies are great, but into the hand of man let me not fall."
So Havayah sent a pestilence upon Yisroel, and there fell from Yisroel seventy thousand men.

And Elokim sent an angel to Yerushalayim to destroy it, and as he destroyed, Havayah saw and regretted the evil, and He said to the destroying angel, "It is enough; now stay your hand," and the angel of Havayah was standing by the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yevusi.

And Dovid lifted his eyes and saw the angel of Havayah standing between the earth and the sky, with a drawn sword in his hand, extended over Yerushalayim, and Dovid and the elders, covered with sackcloth, fell upon their faces.

And Dovid said to Elokim, "Did I not say to count the people? Then I am the one who has sinned, and I have committed evil, but these sheep, what have they done? O Havayah, my Elokim, I beg that Your hand be against me and against my father's house, but not against Your people for a plague."
And the angel of Havayah said to Gad to say to Dovid that Dovid should go up to erect an altar to Havayah in the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yevusi.
And Dovid went up according to the word of Gad that he spoke in the name of Havayah.
And Ornan returned and saw the angel, and his four sons who were with him hid themselves, and Ornan was threshing wheat.
And Dovid came up to Ornan, and Ornan looked and saw Dovid, and he went forth from the threshing-floor, and he bowed down to Dovid with his face to the ground.
And Dovid said to Ornan, "Give me the place of the threshing-floor, so that I may build thereon an altar to Havayah; give it to me for the full price, so that the plague be stayed from the people."

And Ornan said to Dovid, "Take for yourself, and may my master the king do what seems good in his eyes. See, I have given the cattle for burnt offerings, and the threshing tools for [fire] wood, and the wheat for a meal offering; I have given everything."
And King Dovid said to Ornan, "No, for I will buy [it] for the full price, for I will not take what is yours for Havayah, and offer up burnt offerings for nothing."
And Dovid gave to Ornan for the place shekels of gold weighing six hundred.

And Dovid built an altar there to Havayah, and he offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings, and he called out to Havayah, and He answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of the burnt offerings.
And Havayah commanded the angel, and he returned his sword to its sheath.
At that time, when Dovid saw that Havayah had answered him in the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yevusi, he sacrificed there.
And the Tabernacle of Havayah, which Moshe made in the desert, and the altar of the burnt offerings at that time were in the high place in Givon.
But Dovid could not go before it to inquire of Elokim, because he was frightened by the sword of the angel of Havayah.
And Dovid said, "This is the House of Havayah Elokim, and this is the altar for burnt offerings for Yisroel."
And Dovid ordered to gather the strangers who were in the land of Yisroel, and he stationed hewers to hew wrought stone to build the House of Elokim.
And Dovid prepared iron in abundance for the nails, for the doors of the gates, and for the couplings, and copper in abundance, without weight.
And cedar trees without number, for the Tzidonim and the Tzorim brought cedar trees in abundance to Dovid.

And Dovid said, "Shlomo my son is young and tender, and the House to be built for Havayah, [must be] magnified on high for fame and for glory to all lands. I shall [therefore] now make preparation for him." And Dovid prepared in abundance before his death.
And he called Shlomo his son and commanded him to build a House for Havayah Elokim of Yisroel.
And Dovid said to Shlomo, "My son, as for me, it was in my heart to build a House in the name of Havayah my Elokim.
But the word of Havayah was upon me, saying: 'You have shed much blood, and you have waged great wars; you shall not build a House in My Name because you have shed much blood to the ground before Me.

Behold a son will be born to you; he will be a man of peace, and I shall give him peace from all his enemies around about, for Shlomo will be his name, and I shall give peace and quiet to Yisroel in his days.
